headline: Record revenue and profit, outlook lifted despite fuel
summary_short: Carnival Q3 revenue was $8,435M (+3.5% y/y) and net income $1,920M, an all-time high; diluted EPS was $1.40 versus $1.33 a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue rose 3.5% y/y to $8,435M, with net yields in constant currency up 2.4%. Operating income slipped 2.3% y/y to $2,220M as higher fuel prices lifted fuel expense to $615M from $451M. Adjusted EBITDA was flat y/y at $2,993M. Customer deposits reached a third-quarter record. The company redeemed $500M of 7% notes, bought back about $800M of stock since the start of the quarter, and raised its full-year net yield outlook to about 2.3% in constant currency.
confidence_notes: Shard KPIs are SEC-verbatim; the release shows prior-year operating income of $2,271M versus $2,272M on the shard (rounding). Cash and debt figures are from the shard; the release reports debt of $23,912M (current and long-term) at August 31, 2026, a different definition from the shard's long-term debt line. Net income q/q delta computed from shard values. Adjusted EPS of $1.43 and adjusted EBITDA are company non-GAAP measures.

drivers.explanation: Higher fuel prices were the main headwind; fuel expense rose to $615M from $451M, partly offset by lower fuel consumption per ALBD and better cost control.
Net yields in constant currency rose 2.4%, driven by continued demand strength on flat capacity growth.
Adjusted EPS was in line with prior year despite a $0.10 unfavorable net impact from fuel prices and currency rates; lower interest expense and share count also helped GAAP EPS.
The company used cash on hand to redeem $500M of seven percent coupon notes during the quarter.
Management cites accelerating demand, record customer deposits and stronger cost discipline, with full-year adjusted net income improved by more than $150M versus June guidance.
